dnssec_data.cap_broken: DNSSEC is broken: the domain is unreachable for validating resolvers
dnssec_data.issue_bogus: DNSSEC validation fails: validating resolvers refuse to answer for this domain
dnssec_data.issue_ds_mismatch: The DS published at the parent matches none of the zone's DNSKEY keys
dnssec_data.issue_no_dnskey: A DS exists at the parent but the zone publishes no DNSKEY
dnssec_data.issue_no_ds: DNSKEY keys are present but there is no DS at the parent: the chain of trust is not established
dnssec_data.issue_no_rrsig: No signature (RRSIG) on the zone's records
dnssec_data.issue_short_key: RSA key too short ({bits} bits, key tag {key_tag})
dnssec_data.issue_unvalidated: Zone is signed but not validated by the public resolver
dnssec_data.unavailable: No public resolver answered the DNSSEC queries
finding.dnssec_data.broken: DNSSEC is broken for this domain: validating resolvers can no longer resolve it. Fix the signatures or remove the DS at the registrar.
finding.dnssec_data.no_ds: The zone is signed but no DS is published at the parent: DNSSEC has no effect. Publish the DS at the registrar.
finding.dnssec_data.unsigned: DNSSEC is not enabled: the domain's DNS answers can be forged without resolvers noticing. Enable zone signing.
finding.dnssec_data.weak_algorithm: DNSSEC uses a discouraged algorithm ({algorithms}): move to ECDSA P-256 (13) or Ed25519 (15).
module.dnssec_data.checks: Checks the DNSSEC chain of trust: DNSKEY keys, the DS record at the parent and its real match, signatures, validation by a public resolver, broken chain, NSEC/NSEC3. Grade from A to F.
module.dnssec_data.fix:
Identify your case in the finding: unsigned domain (no key), signed zone with no DS at the parent (DNSSEC has no effect), broken chain (domain unreachable for validating resolvers) or deprecated algorithm. A broken chain is the most urgent.
Broken chain: if you have just changed DNS host or disabled DNSSEC, first delete the DS record at the registrar; the domain becomes resolvable again once the DS TTL has passed (often 24 hours). If the cause is an expired signature or a missing key, have your DNS host re-sign the zone.
Unsigned domain: enable DNSSEC at the DNS host that serves your zone ("DNSSEC" option or zone signing); it generates the keys and gives you the DS values (key tag, algorithm, digest type, digest).
Publish this DS at the registrar (DNSSEC or DS section of the domain name), exactly as provided; without it, the chain of trust does not exist. When the DNS host is also the registrar, it is sometimes a simple checkbox.
Deprecated algorithm or digest (RSA/SHA-1, SHA-1 DS digest, RSA key under 2048 bits): move to ECDSA P-256 (algorithm 13) or Ed25519 (algorithm 15) following your host's algorithm rollover procedure; only remove the old DS once the new one is published and propagated.
NSEC3 with iterations: bring their number down to 0, as RFC 9276 recommends (a setting of your DNS host or server).
Before any domain transfer or DNS host change: remove the DS (or follow the transfer procedure with DNSSEC), change name servers, then re-enable DNSSEC.
Check with the commands in the snippet: `dig +short DS example.com` must return the DS, and the answer to `dig +dnssec example.com SOA @1.1.1.1` must carry the `ad` flag. Then run the scan again.
module.dnssec_data.title: DNSSEC
module.dnssec_data.why: DNSSEC prevents forging the domain's DNS answers (cache poisoning, redirection to a fake server). Misconfigured, it also makes the domain unreachable for validating resolvers.
